    let r : ℝ := (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) * ((s - 1) / (s + 1))
    let ℓ : ℝ := (4 * (n : ℝ) * s + (s - 1) ^ 2) /
      (8 * (n : ℝ) * ((n : ℝ) - 1))
    let j0 : Fin n := ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩
    let c : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) :=
      fun O => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) i j0)
    let ν : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) := (Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))).map c
    let f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun y =>
      ((s + 1) * WithLp.ofLp y j0 - (s - 1)) /
        (1 + r ^ 2 - 2 * r * WithLp.ofLp y j0) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)
    let γ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
      fun O => ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
        (((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose))⁻¹
    IsProbabilityMeasure ν ∧
      (∀ᵐ y ∂ν, ‖y‖ = 1) ∧
      (∀ Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        ν.map (fun y => Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin n) (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) y) = ν) ∧
      Integrable f ν ∧
      (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
          (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 2) ∂γ O)
        ∂(Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ)))) =
        (((-1 : ℝ) ^ (n - 1) * (s - 1) ^ (n - 1)) / (s + 1) ^ n) *
          (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) * (∫ y, f y ∂ν)

blind_reconstruction.text:
For every natural number n with 3 ≤ n and every real number κ with 4 ≤ κ, work in E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), with its genuine Euclidean l2 norm, and in the full real orthogonal group G = O(n), including both determinant signs, with the inherited matrix Borel structure. Let H be the literal measure Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts G), namely Haar probability normalized on the entire compact group. Put s = √κ, r = (1 − 1/n)((s − 1)/(s + 1)), and ℓ = (4ns + (s − 1)²)/(8n(n − 1)), where occurrences of n in these arithmetic formulas are real coercions. Let j₀ be the index 0 in Fin n. Define c : G → E by c(O) = WithLp.toLp 2 (i ↦ Oᵢⱼ₀), the Euclidean vector given by the zeroth column of O, and define ν to be exactly the pushforward H.map c.

For every y ∈ E write y₀ = WithLp.ofLp y j₀ and define the real-valued function f on the whole ambient Euclidean space by f(y) = ((s + 1)y₀ − (s − 1))/(1 + r² − 2ry₀)^(n/2). Here n/2 is a real exponent and this expression uses the standard totalized real division and real-power operations, including at ambient points where ordinary positive-base interpretations do not apply. For every O ∈ G let A(O) = ((κ + 1)/2) • I − ((κ − 1)/4) • (O + Oᵀ), let C(O) be its existing nonsingular matrix inverse A(O)⁻¹, and define γ(O) to be literally ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : E) C(O). This is the existing pushforward of canonical stdGaussian by the continuous linear map obtained from the existing totalized positive matrix square root of C(O), with the usual positive-semidefinite-domain meaning; no replacement measure is part of the statement.

Then all of the following hold together: ν is a probability measure; ‖y‖ = 1 for ν-almost every y ∈ E; for every Q ∈ G the pushforward of ν by y ↦ Matrix.toEuclideanCLM(Q)(y), that is ordinary multiplication Qy, equals ν; and f is absolutely Bochner L1 integrable with respect to ν. In addition, the following exact identity of real integrals holds:

∫[O ∈ G] det(O) (∫[x ∈ E] exp(−ℓ‖x‖²) dγ(O)(x)) dH(O)
= (((−1)^(n − 1) (s − 1)^(n − 1))/(s + 1)^n) (1 − 1/n)^(n/2) (∫[y ∈ E] f(y) dν(y)).

The outer integral is over the entire orthogonal group under H, and for each O the inner integral is over all E under γ(O). The final integral is over all E under the literal column pushforward ν. The exponents n − 1 in the sign and numerator powers use natural subtraction; n in (s + 1)^n is a natural exponent; n/2 in both real-power expressions is real. The norm in the Gaussian integral and in the almost-everywhere assertion is the Euclidean norm. The only independent parameters are n and κ with the stated bounds: s, r, ℓ, c, ν, f, and γ are the explicit dependent definitions above, H depends on n, and there are no unspecified constants or additional quantifiers over measures, functions, or parameters.

The almost-everywhere sphere assertion is not an assertion that every ambient y has unit norm. The probability, almost-everywhere support, and orthogonal pushforward invariance assertions do not state any additional identification of ν with a separately defined sphere or surface measure. Integrability is asserted for f under ν; no separate outer- or inner-integrability clause is stated. The theorem does not assert global positivity of the displayed denominator, global continuity of f, or an additional positive-definiteness conclusion about A(O) or C(O). It states the displayed exact integral relation and does not separately supply a value for either side or for the final integral.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.PoissonNormalization
open Matrix MeasureTheory
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.OrthogonalHaar
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantFamily
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.ColumnTransport
set_option autoImplicit false
/-!
Actual full-Haar first-column law and selected Gaussian integral transport.
This is the bounded source-implicit adapter preceding Appendix A.1 in the
proof of Zhou--Suzuki arXiv:2610.20492v1 B.7. It does not identify canonical
normalized surface measure or evaluate either Poisson integral.
-/
theorem selected_column_transport {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ}
    (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) :
    let s : ℝ := Real.sqrt κ
    let r : ℝ := (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) * ((s - 1) / (s + 1))
    let ℓ : ℝ := (4 * (n : ℝ) * s + (s - 1) ^ 2) /
      (8 * (n : ℝ) * ((n : ℝ) - 1))
    let j0 : Fin n := ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩
    let c : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) :=
      fun O => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) i j0)
    let ν : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) := (orthogonalHaar n).map c
    let f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun y =>
      ((s + 1) * WithLp.ofLp y j0 - (s - 1)) /
        (1 + r ^ 2 - 2 * r * WithLp.ofLp y j0) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)
    let γ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
      fun O => ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
        (singleBlockPrecision κ O)⁻¹
    IsProbabilityMeasure ν ∧
      (∀ᵐ y ∂ν, ‖y‖ = 1) ∧
      (∀ Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        ν.map (fun y => Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin n) (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) y) = ν) ∧
      Integrable f ν ∧
      (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
          (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 2) ∂γ O)
        ∂orthogonalHaar n) =
        (((-1 : ℝ) ^ (n - 1) * (s - 1) ^ (n - 1)) / (s + 1) ^ n) *
          (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) * (∫ y, f y ∂ν) := by
  classical
  let s : ℝ := Real.sqrt κ
  let r : ℝ := (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) * ((s - 1) / (s + 1))
  let ℓ : ℝ := (4 * (n : ℝ) * s + (s - 1) ^ 2) /
    (8 * (n : ℝ) * ((n : ℝ) - 1))
  let j0 : Fin n := ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩
  let c : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) :=
    fun O => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) i j0)
  let ν : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) := (orthogonalHaar n).map c
  let f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ := fun y =>
    ((s + 1) * WithLp.ofLp y j0 - (s - 1)) /
      (1 + r ^ 2 - 2 * r * WithLp.ofLp y j0) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)
  let γ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
    fun O => ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
      (singleBlockPrecision κ O)⁻¹
  change IsProbabilityMeasure ν ∧ (∀ᵐ y ∂ν, ‖y‖ = 1) ∧
    (∀ Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
      ν.map (fun y => Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin n)
        (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) y) = ν) ∧ Integrable f ν ∧ _
  have hc : Continuous c :=
    (PiLp.continuous_toLp 2 (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ)).comp
      (continuous_pi (fun i => continuous_subtype_val.matrix_elem i j0))
  have hf : Measurable f := by dsimp [f]; fun_prop
  let := (orthogonalHaar_spec n).1
  have hprob : IsProbabilityMeasure ν := Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map hc.measurable.aemeasurable
  have hnorm (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) : ‖c O‖ = 1 := by
    have hu := Unitary.map_mem (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin n)) O.property
    have hh := ContinuousLinearMap.norm_map_of_mem_unitary hu (PiLp.single 2 j0 (1 : ℝ))
    have he : Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin n)
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (PiLp.single 2 j0 (1 : ℝ)) = c O := by
      apply (WithLp.equiv 2 (Fin n → ℝ)).injective
      change (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ Pi.single j0 1 = fun i =>
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) i j0
      rw [Matrix.mulVec_single_one]
      rfl
    rw [he] at hh
    simpa [PiLp.norm_single] using hh
  have hsphere : ∀ᵐ y ∂ν, ‖y‖ = 1 :=
    (ae_map_iff hc.measurable.aemeasurable
      (isClosed_eq continuous_norm continuous_const).measurableSet).2
        (Filter.Eventually.of_forall hnorm)
  have hinvariant (Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
      ν.map (fun y => Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin n)
        (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) y) = ν := by
    let T := Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin n)
      (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
    have heq : (fun y => T y) ∘ c = c ∘ (fun O => Q * O) := by
      funext O
      apply (WithLp.equiv 2 (Fin n → ℝ)).injective
      ext i
      simp [T, c, Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct]
    change ((orthogonalHaar n).map c).map (fun y => T y) = (orthogonalHaar n).map c
    rw [Measure.map_map T.continuous.measurable hc.measurable, heq,
      ← Measure.map_map hc.measurable (measurable_const_mul Q), orthogonalHaar_map_mul_left]
  have hp := PoissonNormalization.selected_gaussian_normalization hn hκ
  change Integrable (f ∘ c) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧ _ at hp
  have hL : Integrable f ν :=
    (integrable_map_measure hf.aestronglyMeasurable hc.measurable.aemeasurable).2 hp.1
  refine ⟨hprob, hsphere, hinvariant, hL, ?_⟩
  rw [integral_map hc.measurable.aemeasurable hL.aestronglyMeasurable]
  exact hp.2

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.ColumnTransport

steps.title: Use the actual column pushforward
steps.text: Each matrix entry varies continuously with O. The Euclidean identification preserves this continuity, so the column map is measurable and pushes the existing full-Haar probability to a probability.
steps.lean: hc uses PiLp.continuous_toLp and continuous matrix entries. hprob consumes the identical OrthogonalHaar.orthogonalHaar_spec and canonical Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map.

steps.title: Prove genuine Euclidean sphere support
steps.text: Transport the orthogonal matrix through the canonical star-algebra equivalence to Euclidean continuous linear maps. Its unitary norm-preservation acts on the first unit basis vector. The resulting column has norm one for every O, hence also almost surely under its pushforward.
steps.lean: hnorm calls Unitary.map_mem and ContinuousLinearMap.norm_map_of_mem_unitary on Matrix.toEuclideanCLM, then Matrix.mulVec_single_one and PiLp.norm_single. hsphere applies ae_map_iff to the measurable norm level set. No l-infinity norm proxy is used.

steps.title: Preserve the full orthogonal action
steps.text: The actual matrix action commutes with taking the first column by left multiplication. Full Haar invariance, including reflections, therefore gives invariance of the literal column law. This alone is not an identification with canonical surface measure.
steps.lean: hinvariant proves the exact equivariance identity, reuses Measure.map_map twice and calls the identical compiled OrthogonalHaar.orthogonalHaar_map_mul_left. Q is an arbitrary element of full O(n), not SO(n).

steps.title: Transport absolute integrability on the actual support
steps.text: The normalized scalar Haar kernel is exactly f composed with c. Its existing absolute integrability transfers through the measurable pushforward. The ambient quotient is Borel measurable; no off-sphere positivity or continuity is asserted.
steps.lean: hf is global Borel measurability of the literal totalized real quotient. hp consumes the identical PoissonNormalization.selected_gaussian_normalization; hL uses integrable_map_measure with its actual L1 conclusion and the proved measurable c. Positivity and the chosen tilt are supplied by the existing producer, never extra hypotheses.

steps.title: Keep the actual Gaussian expectation attached
steps.text: Use change of variables for the same absolutely integrable function. Substitute the transported integral into the existing selected Gaussian normalization. The focused consumer performs the same substitution in the actual determinant-conditioned Gaussian bind-mixture expectation gap, retaining its factor two.
steps.lean: The final equality directly uses integral_map and hp.2. Tests.GaussianComplexityColumnTransport composes this exact declaration with MixtureExpectation.actual_mixture_expectation_gap; neither a canonical sphere law nor a Poisson value is assumed.
